title: The Wealthy Rancher
html:
• Sutta Nipāta 1.2 Anthology of Discourses 1.2 Sutta Nipāta

Dhaniyasutta The Wealthy Rancher Discourse to Dhaniya

“Pakkodano duddhakhīrohamasmi, “I’ve boiled my rice and drawn my milk,” “I have prepared cooked rice and fresh milk,” (iti dhaniyo gopo) said Dhaniya the rancher, said Dhaniya the Cowherd, Anutīre mahiyā samānavāso; “I stay with my family along the bank of the Mahī. “I stay constantly at the shore of the great river, Channā kuṭi āhito gini, My hut is roofed, my sacred fire kindled: “I have a closed hut with a fire kindled; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Akkodhano vigatakhilohamasmi, “I boil not with anger and have drawn out hard-heartedness,” “I have no anger and no corruption,” (iti bhagavā) said the Buddha, said the Buddha, Anutīre mahiyekarattivāso; “I stay for one night along the bank of the Mahī. “I stay one night at the shore of the great river, Vivaṭā kuṭi nibbuto gini, My hut is wide open, my fire is quenched: “I have an open hut with the fire extinguished; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Andhakamakasā na vijjare, “No gadflies or mosquitoes are found,” “There are no gadflies or mosquitoes,” (iti dhaniyo gopo) said Dhaniya, said Dhaniya the Cowherd, Kacche rūḷhatiṇe caranti gāvo; “cows graze on the lush meadow grass. “In the marshes and meadows where the cattle roam, Vuṭṭhimpi saheyyumāgataṁ, They get by even when the rain comes: “When it rained in the past, they could endure; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Baddhāsi bhisī susaṅkhatā, “I bound a raft and prepared it well,” “The raft was assembled and well-contructed,” (iti bhagavā) said the Buddha, said the Buddha, Tiṇṇo pāragato vineyya oghaṁ; “and with it I crossed over, went to the far shore, and dispelled the flood. “It crossed over to the far shore, it went past the deluge; Attho bhisiyā na vijjati, Now I have no need for a raft: “I have no need of a raft; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Gopī mama assavā alolā, “My wife is obedient, not wanton,” “My cowherd-woman listens and is prudent,” (iti dhaniyo gopo) said Dhaniya, said Dhaniya the Cowherd, Dīgharattaṁ saṁvāsiyā manāpā; “long have we lived together happily. “For a long time, she has been a pleasant co-resident, Tassā na suṇāmi kiñci pāpaṁ, I hear nothing bad about her: “I have never heard anything evil from her; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Cittaṁ mama assavaṁ vimuttaṁ, “My mind is obedient and freed,” “My mind is unpolluted and liberated,” (iti bhagavā) said the Buddha, said the Buddha, Dīgharattaṁ paribhāvitaṁ sudantaṁ; “long nurtured and well-tamed. “For a long time, it has been thoroughly developed and well-trained, Pāpaṁ pana me na vijjati, Nothing bad is found in me: “No evil can be found in me; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Attavetanabhatohamasmi, “I am self-employed,” “I have a servant that I hired myself,” (iti dhaniyo gopo) said Dhaniya, said Dhaniya the Cowherd, Puttā ca me samāniyā arogā; “and my healthy children likewise. “My children are all equally healthy, Tesaṁ na suṇāmi kiñci pāpaṁ, I hear nothing bad about them: “I have never heard anything evil from them; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Nāhaṁ bhatakosmi kassaci, “I am no one’s lackey,” “I am not the servant of anyone,” (iti bhagavā) said the Buddha, said the Buddha, Nibbiṭṭhena carāmi sabbaloke; “with what I have earned I wander the world. “I travel the entire world with what I have gained, Attho bhatiyā na vijjati, I have no need for wages: “I have no need of wages; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Atthi vasā atthi dhenupā, “I have heifers and sucklings,” “There is a cow and a suckling calf,” (iti dhaniyo gopo) said Dhaniya, said Dhaniya the Cowherd, Godharaṇiyo paveṇiyopi atthi; “cows in calf and breeding cows. “There is the herd-mother with her offspring, Usabhopi gavampatīdha atthi, I’ve also got a bull, captain of the herd here: “The father-bull as well; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Natthi vasā natthi dhenupā, “I have no heifers or sucklings,” “There is no cow and no suckling calf,” (iti bhagavā) said the Buddha, said the Buddha, Godharaṇiyo paveṇiyopi natthi; “no cows in calf or breeding cows. “No herd-mother and no offspring, Usabhopi gavampatīdha natthi, I haven’t got a bull, captain of the herd here: “And no father-bull as well; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Khilā nikhātā asampavedhī, “The stakes are driven in, unshakable,” “The post is firmly entrenched and does not wobble,” (iti dhaniyo gopo) said Dhaniya, said Dhaniya the Cowherd, Dāmā muñjamayā navā susaṇṭhānā; “The grass halters are new and well-woven, “The ropes are made of new and well-made twine, Na hi sakkhinti dhenupāpi chettuṁ, not even the sucklings can break them: “It is not possible for the calves to break them; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

“Usabhoriva chetva bandhanāni, “Like a bull I broke the bonds,” “Like a bull that has broken its bonds,” (iti bhagavā) said the Buddha, said the Buddha, Nāgo pūtilataṁva dālayitvā; “like an elephant I snapped the vine. “Like an elephant that has burst through rotten vines, Nāhaṁ punupessaṁ gabbhaseyyaṁ, I will never lie in a womb again: “I will never again enter a womb; Atha ce patthayasī pavassa deva”. so rain forth, heavens, if you wish.” “So if the angels wish, they can make it rain.”

Ninnañca thalañca pūrayanto, Right then a vast cloud rained forth, Flooding both the low ground and the high ground, Mahāmegho pavassi tāvadeva; soaking the uplands and valleys. a great raincloud poured down rain. Sutvā devassa vassato, Hearing the heavens rain down, After hearing the rain from the angels, Imamatthaṁ dhaniyo abhāsatha. Dhaniya said this: Dhaniya spoke about this:

“Lābhā vata no anappakā, “It is no small gain for us “It is a gain for us, and not a small one, Ye mayaṁ bhagavantaṁ addasāma; that we have seen the Buddha. “That we have seen the Buddha; Saraṇaṁ taṁ upema cakkhuma, We come to you for refuge, Clear-eyed One. “I take refuge in the Seer, Satthā no hohi tuvaṁ mahāmuni. O great sage, please be our Teacher. “Great Sage, be our teacher.

Gopī ca ahañca assavā, My wife and I, obedient, “I am a cow-herd, and I listen, Brahmacariyaṁ sugate carāmase; shall lead the spiritual life under the Holy One. “I will live the spiritual life following the Sublime One, Jātimaraṇassa pāragū, Gone beyond birth and death, “To go beyond birth and death, Dukkhassantakarā bhavāmase”. we shall make an end of suffering.” “And bring suffering to an end.”

“Nandati puttehi puttimā, “Children bring you delight!” “One who has children delights because of their children,” (iti māro pāpimā) said Māra the Wicked, said Māra the Evil One, Gomā gohi tatheva nandati; “Cattle also bring you delight! “One who has cattle delights because of their cattle, Upadhī hi narassa nandanā, For attachments are a man’s delight; “Possessions are the delight of a person, Na hi so nandati yo nirūpadhi”. without attachments there’s no delight.” “One who has no possessions has no delight.”

“Socati puttehi puttimā, “Your children bring you sorrow,” “One who has children sorrows because of their children,” (iti bhagavā) said the Buddha, said the Buddha, Gomā gohi tatheva socati; “Your cattle also bring you sorrow. “One who has cattle sorrows because of their cattle, Upadhī hi narassa socanā, For attachments are a man’s sorrow; “Possessions are the the sorrow of a person, Na hi so socati yo nirūpadhī”ti. without attachments there are no sorrows.” “One who has no possessions has no sorrow.”

Dhaniyasuttaṁ dutiyaṁ.
